primitives.name: Flattened Tensor Storage Format
primitives.verbatim_quote: **FTSF** (Flattened Tensor Storage Format, dense tensors): chunk the tensor along its last D_c dimensions; one row per chunk with (id, chunk BINARY, dim_count, dimensions, chunk_dim_count).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_c': 'integer, number of dimensions to chunk', 'id': 'string, unique identifier for chunk', 'chunk_B': 'binary, serialized chunk data', 'dim_count': 'integer, total tensor dimensions', 'dimensions': 'tuple, shape of tensor', 'chunk_dim_count': 'integer, dimensions of chunk'}
primitives.assumptions: Tensor is dense, chunking occurs along last D_c dimensions, metadata is dictionary-encoded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When tensor size exceeds memory limits or when full tensor reads are required.

layer2.mapping: Maps dense tensor slices to indexed chunks in Delta Lake, enabling efficient partial reads and version control.
layer2.telemetry: Chunk read latency, storage size reduction ratio

primitives.name: Compressed Sparse Fiber
primitives.verbatim_quote: **CSF** (Compressed Sparse Fiber): tree-structured compression of duplicate indices per dimension; first two dimensions' fiber pointers/indices stored unchunked per tensor, remaining dimensions chunked.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'fiber_ptr': 'pointer, index into fiber list', 'fiber_idx': 'integer, index within fiber', 'nonzero_count': 'integer, count of non-zero elements', 'sparsity_ratio': 'dimensionless, ratio of zeros to total elements'}
primitives.assumptions: Sparsity ratio below 10%, duplicate indices compress well, access patterns are local.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sparsity exceeds 10% or when fiber structures become too nested.

layer2.mapping: Encodes sparse tensors by compressing shared indices across fibers, reducing I/O for low-density signals.

primitives.name: Block Sparse Generic Storage
primitives.verbatim_quote: **BSGS** (Block Sparse Generic Storage): Mode-Generic format — partition into dense blocks of any order, store non-null blocks + block indices; enables slicing without reading the whole tensor.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'block_order': 'integer, number of dimensions in block', 'block_indices': 'array, coordinates of non-null blocks', 'block_data': 'tensor, values of non-null blocks'}
primitives.assumptions: Blocks are dense, tensor can be partitioned into fixed-size blocks, slicing is supported.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When block sizes are not aligned with access patterns or when memory constraints limit block count.

layer2.mapping: Enables block-level slicing and efficient storage of structured sparse tensors by indexing non-null blocks.

The core insight of the paper is that naive tensor serialization incurs significant redundancy due to zero-padding in dense tensors and inefficient access in sparse ones. The proposed layouts—FTSF, CSR/CSC, CSF, and BSGS—are designed to address these inefficiencies by leveraging chunking, sparse encodings, and structure-aware storage. FTSF optimizes dense tensors by flattening and chunking along dimensions, allowing for localized reads. CSR/CSC adapts matrix-based sparse formats to higher-order tensors, while CSF uses hierarchical index compression for extreme sparsity. BSGS generalizes block-based storage to arbitrary tensor orders. These primitives enable GSE to perform efficient batch reads and maintain versioned embeddings without blob overhead. Failure modes include performance degradation under high sparsity or mismatched access patterns. The mathematical duality lies in mapping between flat representations and structured views of tensors, which is essential for scalable machine learning pipelines in lakehouse architectures.
